##  Sixty Years of Traditions in Glassmaking, Combined with the Most Modern Technology
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
With over 60 years of history in the glassmaking, Rubin is one of the most advanced and established glass producers in the Balkan region. We combine our vast experience and traditions with the latest technological advancements in the industry to produce glass packaging of perfect quality.
[ Learn more ](https://rubin-glass.eu/history/)
##  Rubin  Design Glass Center
##  Proven Craftsmanship  and Modern Innovation for Exceptional Quality!
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Design and innovation in the development of high-quality glass products on a world-class level. With a legacy of excellence, we bring unparalleled expertise in manufacturing glassware for various market segments. Our commitment to cutting-edge technology, precision craftsmanship and sustainable production ensures that we deliver premium glass solutions tailored to the evolving needs of industries worldwide.
[ Learn more ](https://rubin-glass.eu/desgin-glass-center/)

##  New  Products
##  Quality, Sustainability and Technology. Smart, innovative solutions for the market!
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Our glass products are used in various industries, offering reliability and functionality. We focus on sustainable manufacturing, minimizing waste, and optimizing resource use. Innovation drives our growth and we expand our range with advanced, efficient solutions. We work closely with partners to provide customized products that meet specific needs. Our flexibility allows us to be a trusted supplier across industries. RUBIN continues to grow, driving innovation with modern technologies and expanding its market presence.

#### LOCATION
The Rubin Factory is situated in the industrial hub of Pleven, Northern Bulgaria. Our strategic location offers several logistical advantages, ensuring efficient transportation and distribution:
  * **Proximity to the A2 Hemus Highway** for seamless road connectivity.
  * **Close access to the national railway network (BDZ)** , with an internal railway system on-site, facilitating efficient train shipments.
  * **Near the Danube River** , enabling cost-effective and reliable maritime shipping.


We pride ourselves on being well-connected to key transport networks, ensuring swift and reliable delivery of our products.

##  Reliable  fuel system
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
The furnaces are powered by a top-notch fuel system that uses gas and methane. That system contributes to producing glass with a homogeneous mixture and high-quality composition.
##  Electric  system
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
A complementary electric heating system is installed on all furnaces , which contributes to precise control of the melting and the homogenizing process.
## Forming
##  Precise  molding machines
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
The forming process relies on the latest servo engines and mechanisms, which guarantee a precise workflow and quality of the product.
##  Triple gob technology 
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Every molding machine can work in a Blow & Blow, Press & Blow, and Narrow Neck Press & Blow mode to produce, respectively, standard bottles, jars, and lightweight bottles.
![Asset 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20512'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

##  Production  lines
##  Straight lines
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
All the production lines are built to be predominantly straight, resulting in a faster product flow and more secure transportation. Because of their configuration flexibility, most of our lines are capable of producing intricate products.
##  OMEGA  technology
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Our production process allows our company to be easily certified by worldwide brands since we have an OMEGA system on every line, which allows the product to be turned upside down and blown out with compressed air. This makes our production lines meet the requirements to produce even baby food containers.

##  Real-time  online control

##  Rubin's Vision: Investment Towards a Sustainable and Innovative Future in the Glass Industry
Rubin is excited to launch a new investment program to further our commitment to sustainability, innovation, and growth. This program aims to expand our renewable energy capacity, enhance water conservation efforts, and increase our average recycled content while focusing on employee development and operational efficiency. Through this strategic initiative, we aim to lead the way in sustainable practices within the glass industry, underlining our commitment to both our customers and the environment.
##  Facility  Details
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Rubin’s new production facility is a testament to our commitment to innovation in the glass industry. The facility features Furnace 3, which has a daily capacity of 300 tons.
SORG – renowned for its innovative approach towards overcoming industry challenges and advancing technology is the company responsible for the development of Rubin’s Furnace 3.
The collaboration between Rubin and SORG has led to the integration of cutting-edge technology in Furnace 3, enabling us to manufacture top-notch glass products while minimizing our environmental footprint.
![Картина4](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20602'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

##  Strategic ​Partnership 
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
In a significant development, Rubin has formed a strategic partnership with cm.project.ing GmbH, an independent consultant based in Germany. This partnership aims to bring additional layers of expertise, particularly in the domains of project engineering, data analytics, and sustainable practices.
CM.PROJECT.ING has played a pivotal role in bringing the best enterprises in the glass industry to life. With an impressive track record, the CM.PROJECT.ING team serves as trusted advisors for significant projects worldwide.
##  Smart Operations and Data Analysis
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## History of Rubin Glass Factory
##  Sixty years of traditions in glassmaking, combined with the most modern technology
With over 60 years of history in glassmaking, Rubin is one of the most advanced and established glass producers in the Balkan region. We combine our vast experience and traditions with the latest technological advancements in the industry to produce glass packaging of perfect quality.
1965
##### The Beginning of Glass Production
In July 1965, glass packaging production began in the city of Pleven under the name **_"Gen. Ivan Vinarov."_** The official inauguration took place on November 10 of the same year. The factory started operations with two main production workshops, each equipped with two glass furnaces and a total of 17 production lines. Three furnaces operated with clear glass, and one with colored (green) glass.
1965
1972
##### Expansion into the Largest Facility in the Balkans
The design and construction of a new workshop began, featuring two larger glass furnaces, each equipped with six production lines. As a result of this development, the factory became the largest producer of packaging glass in the Balkan Peninsula at that time, specializing in bottles and jars.
1972
1975
##### Transition to Natural Gas for Greater Efficiency
The factory transitioned to natural gas via a gasification process, replacing liquid fuels. This resulted in a significant improvement in energy efficiency and production sustainability.
1975
1985
##### Peak Industrial Growth and Workforce Expansion
At its peak, the facility operated five active furnaces and 26 production lines. The workforce exceeded 1,500 employees, establishing the factory as a key industrial center in the Pleven region.
1985
1991
##### Rebranding as “RUBIN”
The factory officially adopted the name “RUBIN,” which remains its registered trade name to this day.
1991
2007
##### Full Modernization of Clear Glass Production
A large-scale investment was made to fully renovate and modernize of the production equipment in the clear glass facility. This step introduced new technologies, resulting in productivity and enhanced product quality.
2007
2012
##### Upgrade of the Colored Glass Unit
A new investment was made to fully upgrade the colored glass production unit. The main equipment was replaced, and innovative solutions to optimize production processes were introduced.
2012
2015
##### Streamlined Production with Two Furnaces
As of this year, the factory operates two production furnaces — one for clear glass and one for colored — serviced by seven production lines. The total annual production capacity exceeds 190 million glass containers.
2015
2018–2020
##### Technological Leap and Infrastructure Growth
New infrastructure and technological upgrades were realized, as part of a major investment project. This included the delivery and installation of a raw materials conveyor system, the construction of recycling systems (closed-loop cycle), the expansion of production buildings, and the commissioning of two high-efficiency furnaces — No. 5 and No. 6 — for clear and colored glass.  
  
In July 2018, Furnace No. 6 was launched — a new-generation installation for colored glass, developed by the German company SORG. In March 2020, Furnace No. 5 was also put into operation for the production of clear packaging glass. The combined capacity of both furnaces reaches 450 tons of molten glass per 24 hours. 
2018–2020
2023
##### Largest Expansion in Company History
A new large-scale project has been initiated to expand production capacity with the construction of an additional high-performance Furnace No. 3, with a capacity exceeding 300 tons of glass per day. The project includes a complete overhaul of the raw materials facility and related infrastructure for the delivery, the storage, and the dosing of materials.  
  
Plans include the modernization of Workshop No. 1 with the installation of four new glass-forming machines, next-generation annealing furnaces, and advanced equipment for automated quality inspection. An expanded warehouse module for storage and handling of finished products is also under construction.  
  
Upon completion and commissioning of the new furnace, RUBIN GLASS FACTORY will operate with three high-efficiency furnaces and a total of 11 production lines — the highest production capacity in the company’s 60-year history. This achievement further strengthens the factory’s position as a leading manufacturer of packaging glass in the region, with a clear focus on sustainable growth, quality, and long-term industrial partnerships. 
2023
2025
##### 60 Years of Tradition and a New Era
In 2025, Rubin Glass Factory marked its 60th anniversary with the inauguration of Furnace No. 3, a state-of-the-art facility with a production capacity exceeding 300 tons of glass per day. The €125 million investment (equivalent to BGN 250 million), made possible with the support of Postbank and global industry leaders such as Nikolaus Sorg and Emhart Glass, has firmly established the factory as one of Europe's leading packaging glass production centers.   
  
This expansion not only increased production capacity but also led to the creation of over 600 new jobs, ensuring the company's sustainable industrial presence in Northwestern Bulgaria for at least the next 15 years. The inauguration ceremony was attended by prominent figures from the global glass industry, further solidifying Bulgaria's position on the map of the world's glass sector.

**MANAGEMENT POLICY**
In line with its development strategy of Rubin Trading JSC, the implemented Integrated Management System (IMS), compliant with the requirements of ISO 50001:2018, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 22000:2018, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO 22301:2019, and the international certification FSSC 22000 in its part for the production of food packaging, we declare our commitment to achieving the strategic goals:
  * increasing customer satisfaction through continuous improvement of product quality, safety and authenticity management;
  * strengthening the company’s positions in the production and sale of safe glass packaging;
  * continuous improvement of its performance in relation to the environment;
  * ensuring and maintaining healthy and safe working conditions;
  * continuous improvement of energy efficiency, efficient use of energy resources, encouragement the deployment of innovative technologies, equipment and processes that save energy;
  * ensuring the continuity of production and trade with glass packaging.
  * our product safety management system ensures controlled conditions under which hazards to the product and respectively to the food for which it is intended are identified, assessed and controlled in such a way that the products produced could not cause harm directly or indirectly to the final consumer.
  * delivery of the best and safest possible product, within the requirements of customers, observing the rules of good production and hygiene practices, which in turn guarantee the safety of the product, respectively food and the health of consumers.
  * promoting and building a product safety culture in the organization by providing training: Improves communication at all levels of the organization and evaluates achievements in terms of safety and quality of manufactured products.


In pursuance of the set goals, the management of the enterprise assumes personal responsibility for the efficient functioning of the implemented management systems and undertakes to:
  * sets and reviews objectives for quality, product safety, environment, occupational health and safety, business continuity and general and specific energy goals;
  * provide the resources and information necessary to achieve the objectives;
  * manage the activities within the scope of each of the implemented systems, in accordance with the applicable legislation and all commitments, as well as in accordance with international management standards;
  * manage environmental protection, including pollution prevention in terms of efficient waste management, use of appropriate technologies and equipment with minimal negative impact on the environment, sustainable use of resources;
  * creates conditions for managing health and safety at work, preventing injuries, illnesses and accidents;
  * creates conditions for staff awareness of the principles, policies and objectives of the management systems by providing motivation, training and qualification;
  * manage the use of available material, human and financial resources in a way that ensures the efficient functioning of processes and increases the quality and safety of products;
  * works to build mutual trust with customers by satisfying their requirements, based on the correctness, quality and safety of the offered glass packaging;
  * maintains relationships with suppliers, guaranteeing high quality of collaboration;
  * effective use of available resources and in accordance with the requirements, needs and needs of stakeholders:
    * introducing new methods for risk analysis and assessment;
    * methods for hazard forecasting;
    * optimization of processes – adequacy, expediency, quality awareness;
    * control and reduction of the negative impact on the environment during the implementation of processes;


  * maintaining a system for safe production and quality control and critical points in the food production process and compliance with regulations.
  * clearly delegated responsibilities to staff in the organization.


This policy must be implemented, maintained, disseminated, and made it accessible and understandable to all. The commitment of all employees of the company, in accordance with the objectives, through knowledge of the requirements for compliance with internationally recognized quality management standards; customer requirements, as well as all legal and regulatory requirements applicable to our sector.
As Executive Director of Rubin Trading JSC, I declare my personal participation and commitment to maintain and continuously improve the IMS and to implement this policy.

##  Sustainability 
Rubin is fully committed to the resource efficiency and sustainability of its operations. The company has made significant efforts to meet the ecological, sustainable, and resource-efficient production criteria, while adhering to all commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, and the Paris Agreement.
We are proud to announce that by 2023, Rubin has already achieved the goals outlined in both the company’s sustainability program and the national program of Bulgaria for the year 2030.
##  Gas Supply Optimization
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Rubin employs cutting-edge technologies to optimize gas consumption throughout the production process. Innovative techniques and state-of-the-art equipment are integrated into our operations, enabling us to reduce gas usage while maintaining high productivity levels. This not only helps decrease carbon emissions but also enhances the competitiveness and reputation of the company. 
![shutterstock 2126977343](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20442'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
![shutterstock 1771011401 scaled e1747386282539](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20535'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
##  Preserving Water ​Resources
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Rubin adopts rainwater harvesting practices, capturing and utilizing rainwater for various production needs. This innovative approach creates a closed-loop system, where collected water is treated and reused, reducing the reliance on external water sources and promoting sustainable water usage. By implementing this method, Rubin minimizes dependence on the public water supply and helps mitigate the risk of water resource depletion.
##  Green  Energy​
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
Rubin is adopting photovoltaic technology as a core strategy to strengthen its sustainability initiatives. By harnessing solar energy and converting it into usable electricity, Rubin is reducing its reliance on conventional energy sources and minimizing carbon emissions. Currently, the facility has an installed photovoltaic capacity of 2 MW, with plans for a full expansion to meet the company’s energy needs. The anticipated total capacity will reach 10 MW, reinforcing Rubin’s commitment to a more sustainable future.
![1820196929 huge](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20534'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
![shutterstock 580663432](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20532'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
##  Glass ​Recycling​
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
As part of its commitment to sustainable practices, Rubin places significant emphasis on glass recycling. By reintegrating cullet into the production process, the company not only reduces waste but also minimizes the need for raw material input. Recycled glass melts at a lower temperature compared to virgin raw materials, resulting in reduced energy consumption during manufacturing and further lowering the carbon footprint. Additionally, for every ton of cullet used, up to 1.2 tons of raw materials are conserved. This process reflects Rubin’s dedication to a zero-waste production model, ensuring that every product manufactured embodies sustainability and operational efficiency.
##  Modern Chemical  Analysis Laboratory​​
![Layer 11](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20135%202'%3E%3C/svg%3E)
To ensure the highest quality and efficiency in recycling, Rubin has made a substantial investment in a state-of-the-art chemical analysis laboratory. Equipped with the latest technologies, this advanced facility allows for the thorough analysis of the chemical composition of all raw materials, including various types of glass. With this capability, the team can confidently incorporate glass with different chemical compositions into the production process, ensuring that the quality of the final product is never compromised. This investment has enabled Rubin to achieve an impressive 45% recycled content, reaching its 2030 sustainability targets ahead of schedule, in 2023.
